status: Episode-only scene replacement revision.01/02 pairs carried forward unchanged and unapproved; new05 campfire pair pending.
timing_status: Normal-rate actual voice takes measured; visual review pending.
character_identity_rule: Match the original Sol artwork: recognizable compact reference proportions and volume, asymmetric flame silhouette, original red/orange/cream layer relationships, short rounded arms and tiny stubby feet at their original lengths and attachment points. Keep both original eye ovals uniformly navy #1C2447, with the normal open-eye design unchanged in shape, size, low placement and close spacing, without highlights, whites, extra pupils or drift. A brief natural blink is allowed, returning promptly to the original open ovals. Keep him completely mouthless and blank beneath the eyes; no nose, eyebrows, fingers, elongated limbs or separate humanoid torso. Keep the face attached to the body with no separate head or neck. Scripted gaze shifts may move the original ovals coherently as a pair within the face while preserving their normal shape, size and spacing. Settled endpoints retain the reference body form; small coordinated bouncy flame-like flex during the action preserves his recognizable design. Actual wood fire remains separate.
painted_art_direction: Match the approved Ignite artwork: soft, matte gouache-like brushwork, broad simplified shapes, restrained detail, layered color, softened painted edges and subtle paper texture. Paint all subjects and surroundings together with coherent perspective and lighting. Build rounded forms and space through overlapping painted layers, gentle shading and contact shadows. No glossy rendering, generic vector shapes, inked outlines, heavy grain or decorative clutter.

composition_rules.captions: Important action stays above y=76%; lower foreground near y=80–90% stays quiet for editable captions.
composition_rules.character_count: One Sol where specified; no Sol in Scenes 03/04.
composition_rules.eyes: Keep the normal open-eye design as the original navy #1C2447 ovals with their reference shape, size, low resting placement and close spacing. Scripted upward glances may shift the pair coherently within the face. A brief natural blink may close/reopen both eyes, returning promptly to the same gaze and original oval design. No whites, highlights, extra pupils, eyebrows, winks, unrelated eye morphs or facial-feature drift.
composition_rules.narrator_eyeline: MANDATORY whenever Narrator speaks with Sol visible: gaze UP to the fixed voice just above camera before the first word and throughout the turn, with gentle listening idle. A short silent gaze transition may precede voice onset; final windows follow real normal-rate recordings.
composition_rules.fire_distinction: Sol remains the solid reference mascot. Actual fire is a separate faceless painted flame attached to the planned wood or embers, with only localized reflected warmth after ignition.

sources.title: Fire 400 ka — Pathways to Ancient Britain
sources.supports: The research team distinguishes likely use of wildfires and maintained embers from intentional ignition. Early dates are uncertain; no first discoverer is identified.

sources.title: Davis et al. — Earliest evidence of making fire
sources.supports: The study reports evidence interpreted as deliberate fire-making at Barnham around 400,000 years ago. This evidence date is not a known first invention or discoverer.

sources.title: Berna et al. — Fire evidence at Wonderwerk Cave
sources.supports: Burned bone and plant ash document burning in an archaeological context around one million years ago. This does not identify a person or establish the first ignition method.
